line: One snap in, I put some racks in my grill
vault_lines: One snap in, I put some racks in my grill

line: They tellin’ me slow down (Slow down) They gave me a chill pill (Chill out)
vault_lines: They tellin' me slow down (Slow down)
meaning:
Kodak is so energetic at the function that his surrounding associates gave him a “chill pill,” perhaps the anti-anxiety drug Xanax, so he can chill out.

Kodak could also be thugging a little too hard, so the “chill pill” could be a reference to his jail sentence.

line: My homies the real deal We smokin’ that kill-kill She shake it, it feel real
meaning:
“Real deal” implies Swae’s friends are active in the street. “Kill-kill” refers to high grade marijuana.

His girl, however, may not be entirely real, but her surgical enhancements feel organic, and that’s all that matters.

line: I got dressed, left the crib, set the trend
vault_lines: I got dressed, left the crib, set the trend
meaning: Swae and Jxm both have a keen eye for fashion, sporting clothes from street brands to high end luxury items. Every time they go out, the trends follow them.

line: Swag, yeah Frank Lucas with a grill
meaning:
Frank Lucas was a heroin kingpin, importing the drug via a network of conspirators and introducing it into Harlem in the 60s. The 2007 film American Gangster was  based around his story. In addition to notoriety in the crime community, Frank was also known for rocking chinchilla and ballin' with his drug money.

And Jxmmi’s got that Frank Lucas level of swag, with a grill to match.

line: A cool Herc on the Earth
vault_lines: A cool Herc on the Earth
meaning: A reference to DJ Kool Herc, a hip-hop pioneer who brought the genre to The Bronx in the 70s. May also be a reference to the Greek God Hercules, who was known for his globe-trotting adventures.

line: Girl you better put that ass to work Can a nigga hold the cam like Kirk
vault_lines: Girl you better put that ass to work
meaning:
This couplet plays on famed Atlanta photographer and videographer Cam Kirk, who has had his work associated with nearly every major player of the contemporary Atlanta scene.

Possibly his most notable collaborations have come with Gucci Mane, whose own associations with Atlanta artists play like a game of Six Degrees of Separation; their work together inspired his Trap God installation, footage from which led to the creation of the video for Young Thug and Gucci Mane’s “Again.”

line: All I smoke is loud yeah, it’s gon’ blast in your ear Man I’m high as the cloud, I’m on a new atmosphere
vault_lines: All I smoke is loud yeah, it's gon' blast in your ear
meaning: High-grade marijuana is often referred to as “loud,” but Kodak uses wordplay to compare it to an actual noise. Kodak also states that he’s so high that he compares himself to a cloud high in the atmosphere.

line: Because I was Spend Ben (Spend Ben) They know I would Kill Bill (Hit him) I walk round Ben still (Ben still)
vault_lines: Because I was Spend Ben (Spend Ben)
meaning:
Kodak Black is referring to Quentin Tarintino’s fourth film  Kill Bill where the main character, “The Bride,” was apart of the Deadly Viper Assassination Squad and known to be highly skilled with a sword.



Similarly, Kodak carriers around a weapon made of steel (a gun), that he uses to take out his foes.

line: I can’t get a grip, man this bitch a flip Walked in, throwin’ the cash like nerfs
vault_lines: I can't get a grip, man this bitch a flip
meaning: “Benji’s” are hundred dollar bills, named after Benjamin Franklin who adorns the front of the bill. Slim doesn’t have self-control, shooting money off in the strip club like a Nerf Gun.

line: The big watch on, feel like Ben 10
vault_lines: The big watch on, feel like Ben 10
meaning:
Slim and Swae Lee’s first album Sremmlife was a major success, gaining the duo large amounts of money. Slim now has the pockets to afford the finest and biggest of watches.

Ben 10 was an animated TV show that aired in the mid-2000’s on Cartoon Network. In the show, titular character Ben was a young boy who wore a large alien device on his wrist that resembled a watch.

line: Pockets fat, Uncle Phil Girls on me like Will (Mike WiLL)
meaning:
Reference to hit 90s TV sitcom The Fresh Prince of Bel Air. In the show, Uncle Phil was financially comfortable, having “fat pockets” of cash. He was also quite rotund.

Will Smith played “Will”, and was regularly seen with new girlfriends. Slim has the best of both worlds: Uncle Phil’s money and Will’s prolific dating history.
